idea-plugin.name: RefDex
idea-plugin.description:
Give your AI agent a map of your code, and watch it stop reading whole files. 🗺️

RefDex indexes every class, method, function and property in your project and hands that index to your AI agent. Instead of opening a 900-line file to find one method, the agent asks "where is OrderService?", "what's in this file?" or "who calls this?" and gets a short, exact answer. Fewer tokens, sharper answers, and more room in the context window for the work you actually asked for.

How it saves tokens

AI agents learn about your code by reading files. In a big project that means reading lots of code that has nothing to do with the task. RefDex lets them look things up instead:

  • Find a class: get its name, signature, file and line in one answer, instead of searching and opening candidate files.
  • Understand a file: get its outline (imports and signatures, no bodies) instead of the whole file.
  • Read one method: get just that method, fresh from disk, instead of the file around it.
  • Before a change: get every caller, subclass and reference, each with the method it's in.
  • New to a codebase? Get a repo map of the code the rest of the project depends on most, trimmed to a token budget.

For example, a 915-line file costs about 11,000 tokens to read. Its outline costs about 2,600, and a single method about 280. That adds up quickly over a long session:

  • Lower cost, more headroom. Sessions stay under the context limit longer.
  • More focused answers. The context holds the code that matters, not everything near it.
  • Fewer wrong guesses. Signatures, callers and base classes come from parsed code, not from skimming.

And RefDex knows when to step aside. Its tool definitions cost about 1,200 tokens per request, so on a small project, where reading files is cheap anyway, it keeps them switched off. It turns them on once your code is big enough to benefit. The status bar always tells you which applies and why.

Languages

Java, C#, Python and TypeScript (including TSX), with the details big projects need: Java packages, C# namespaces and partial classes, Python packages and src/ layouts, and TypeScript path aliases and barrel files.

AI agents

  • Claude Code: connected in one click, just for you or shared with your team through .mcp.json.
  • Junie: connected in one click through the project's .junie/mcp/mcp.json.
  • GitHub Copilot (agent mode): connected in one click, then restart the IDE.
  • JetBrains AI Assistant: RefDex copies a ready-made config for you to paste into its MCP settings.

Any other agent that speaks the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can use RefDex too.

Why you'll like it

  • Zero fuss. Open a project and RefDex indexes it in the background, without blocking the IDE.
  • Always up to date. When you save a file, only that file is parsed again, in milliseconds.
  • Never stale. Code is read from disk whenever the agent asks, so it always sees what you see.
  • Private. Everything runs on your machine. No code leaves it, and there's no account to create.
  • Nothing else to install. The indexer comes with the plugin.

Getting started

1. Open your project. Install RefDex and open a Java, C#, Python or TypeScript project. RefDex starts in the background right away.

2. Build the index. Click RefDex in the status bar and choose Reindex Project. A 3,000-file project takes under 30 seconds. When it's done, the status bar shows RefDex: N files, and from then on RefDex updates the index by itself whenever you save a file. Hover over it to see the symbol count and whether the AI tools are on for this project.

3. Connect your agent. Choose Tools | RefDex | Connect AI Client… (RefDex also offers this after the first index when the tools are on), then pick your agent:

  • Claude Code: pick Claude Code to keep it private to you, or Claude Code (shared) to add it to the project's .mcp.json for your whole team. Then start a new Claude Code session.
  • Junie: pick Junie. It works in the next Junie session.
  • GitHub Copilot: pick GitHub Copilot, restart the IDE, and use Copilot Chat in agent mode.
  • AI Assistant: pick copy MCP config, then go to Settings | Tools | AI Assistant | Model Context Protocol, click Add and paste the config.

4. Ask away. You don't need special prompts. Your agent learns what the tools are for and uses them on its own. To see it in action, try something like:

  • "Give me an overview of this codebase."
  • "Where is the order validation, and who calls it?"
  • "Rename OrderService.submit to place and update every caller."

5. Fine-tune (optional). In Settings | Tools | RefDex you can choose which files and languages to index, and when the AI tools are offered: automatically by project size, always or never. On a small project, RefDex keeps the tools off until your code grows. Choose Always if you want them anyway.

That's it. Happy coding! 🚀
